scope: 79.9-second final V10 video; six original clips. Event evaluation only; still-image gallery excluded.
status: Post-hoc development review by assistant; not independent human or held-out evaluation.

matching.method: Maximum-cardinality one-to-one temporal matching within clip and semantic key. Duplicate predictions are false positives.
matching.key: event family, team for persons, death/non-death disappearance, exact object class, exact HUD field and before/after values, exact Spike status or effect

annotation.person: Rendered world body, including visible portion, excludes corpse and pure through-wall silhouette. Same person occluded for <0.8s stays one episode.
annotation.disappearance: Last visible time +0.8s; only if within clip. If same visible person has confirmed death, use death event once instead of a later non-death disappearance.
annotation.death: First complete new killfeed row, includes off-screen and spectated ally deaths; initial pre-existing rows excluded.
annotation.objects: First visible presence episode of each supported object class; re-observation after >=0.8s absence is new; multiple simultaneous same-class instances count once. Initial visible object counts at time zero.
annotation.hud: First legible new numeric value. Initial health/ammo are state, not changes. Weapon swaps count numeric magazine changes. Spectated HUD included. First planted-Spike icon is accepted; defuse requires explicit text.
annotation.effects: New recognizable flash/reveal onsets; supported world utilities only. No inferred causes/owners.
annotation.boundary: No disappearance or HUD change manufactured across the six edits.
annotation.method: Raw source overview contact sheets, transition crops and existing source-frame annotations. Added numeric HUD transitions reviewed on consecutive decoded frames. New world timestamps are sampled estimates (typically 0.1–0.25s precision), not second-annotator verified.
annotation.limitations: Supported observable event vocabulary only, not every possible game mechanic. Narrow confidence intervals would be inappropriate for six reused clips.
